en: class for advanced learners; the highest-level class

examples.en: Next semester I'll study in the advanced class.
The advanced class has a lot of discussion.
I did well on the test and moved up to the advanced class.

examples.ko: 고급반에 들어가려면 레벨 테스트를 봐야 해요.
examples.en: To get into the advanced class, you have to take a level test.
The friends in the advanced class speak Korean really well.

examples.ko: 저는 아직 고급반이 아니라서 신문 기사가 어려워요.
examples.en: I'm not in the advanced class yet, so news articles are hard for me.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '초급반', '중급반'이에요. 학원이나 어학당 수업을 말할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I passed the test and moved up to the advanced class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 단계 높은 반으로 옮길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving up to a higher class.
phrases.en_equiv: to move up to the advanced class

phrases.en: I'm studying in the intermediate class now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고급반 바로 아래 단계의 반이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The class level right below 고급반.

phrases.en: The advanced class is hard but fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업 내용이나 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the lessons or atmosphere.

explain_en: Its companions are '초급반' (beginner class) and '중급반' (intermediate class). It is often used for classes at academies and language institutes.

examples.en: When you reach the upper grades of elementary school, the homework increases.
The older girls from the upper grades helped us.
This book is for the upper grades.
The lower grades and the upper grades have different break times.
My younger sibling will soon move up to the upper grades.
It is a slightly difficult problem for the upper grades.

explain: 반대말은 '저학년'이에요. 초등학교에서는 보통 1~2학년을 저학년, 3~4학년을 중학년, 5~6학년을 고학년이라고 불러요. 한 학년이 아니라 여러 학년을 묶어서 가리키는 말이에요.

phrases.en: Upper-grade students have longer classes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '학생'을 붙여 그 학년의 사람들을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 학생 refers to the students in those grades.

phrases.en: The lower grades and upper grades play together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '저학년'과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together with its opposite, 저학년.

phrases.en: My child is in the upper grades now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 아이나 학생이 몇 학년쯤인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say roughly which grades a child is in.

explain_en: The opposite is 저학년 (lower grades). In elementary school, grades 1-2 are usually 저학년, grades 3-4 are 중학년 and grades 5-6 are 고학년. It groups several grades together rather than naming a single one.

examples.en: My friend's handwriting style is really pretty.

examples.ko: 이 글씨체가 읽기 편해서 계속 써요.
examples.en: I keep using this lettering style because it is easy to read.
I looked at my teacher's handwriting and copied it.
The mood changes depending on the lettering style.

examples.ko: 손으로 쓴 것 같은 글씨체로 카드를 꾸몄어요.
examples.en: I decorated the card in a hand-written looking style.

examples.ko: 글씨체까지 닮은 두 사람이 쌍둥이 같아요.
examples.en: The two people look like twins, even down to their handwriting.

explain: '글씨가 예뻐요'는 쓴 솜씨를 칭찬하는 말이고, '글씨체가 예뻐요'는 글자 모양의 스타일을 말해요. 컴퓨터에서는 '글꼴'이나 '폰트'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I changed the font of my presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터에서 쓰는 글자 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This refers to a font on a computer.

phrases.en: I changed my handwriting style to look nicer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자 모양을 다르게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when changing the letter style.

phrases.en: The two people's handwriting is different.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자 모양을 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to compare letter styles.

explain_en: '글씨가 예뻐요' praises how well someone writes, while '글씨체가 예뻐요' talks about the style of the letter shapes. On a computer people say '글꼴' or '폰트'.

en: (couple) to work together; to work for a double income; to work in double harness

examples.ko: 저와 아내는 둘 다 일하니까 맞벌이해요.
examples.en: My wife and I both work, so we are a two-income couple.

examples.ko: 부모님은 오래 맞벌이하셔서 저를 할머니가 키워 주셨어요.
examples.en: My parents both worked for a long time, so my grandmother raised me.
I want us both to keep working even after the baby is born.
Couples who both work share the housework.

examples.ko: 예전에는 맞벌이했지만 지금은 아내가 쉬고 있어요.
examples.en: We both worked before, but now my wife is taking a break.
Housing is expensive, so we have no choice but to both work.

explain: '맞벌이 부부'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요. 반대는 한 사람만 돈을 버는 '외벌이'예요. 주어는 부부나 가족이어서 한 사람이 혼자 '맞벌이해요'라고 하면 어색해요.

phrases.en: Dual-income couples are busy every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사처럼 '부부' 앞에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used before '부부' like a noun.

phrases.en: We both work, so we don't have much time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 이어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to give a reason.

phrases.en: My parents don't both work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 사람만 돈을 벌 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for when only one person earns.
phrases.en_equiv: not to have a double income

explain_en: It also works as a noun, as in '맞벌이 부부'. The opposite is '외벌이', where only one person earns money. The subject is a couple or a family, so one person alone saying '맞벌이해요' sounds odd.

examples.ko: 수업 진도가 너무 빨라서 따라가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The class is moving so fast that it's hard to keep up.
Today we covered the textbook up to page 50.
Teacher, how far have we gotten?
Because of the exam, we rushed to finish the material.

examples.ko: 저는 혼자 공부해서 진도를 마음대로 정해요.
examples.en: I study alone, so I set my own pace.
I was absent and missed the lesson material.

explain: 진도는 수업이나 공부가 어디까지 나아갔는지를 말해요. '진도를 나가다', '진도가 빠르다/느리다'처럼 써요. 일이 얼마나 되었는지는 '진행 상황'이라고 하고, 진도는 주로 공부나 수업에 써요.

phrases.en: This class moves quickly through the material.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업이 빨리 나아갈 때 '진도'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 진도 when a class moves ahead quickly.

phrases.en: I review so that I can keep up with the lessons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업이 나아가는 속도에 맞춰 공부한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means studying at the same pace as the class.
phrases.en_equiv: to keep up with the lessons

phrases.en: Because I was sick, my study progress became slow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공부가 천천히 나아갈 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when studying moves ahead slowly.

explain_en: 진도 is how far a class or study has progressed. It is used as '진도를 나가다' or '진도가 빠르다/느리다'. How far work has gone is '진행 상황'; 진도 is mainly for study and lessons.

en: to enter a higher education institution

examples.en: I'm entering university next year.
My older sister went on to graduate school.
I'm going to enter a school to study art.

examples.ko: 고등학교를 졸업하고 바로 진학하는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: Many students go straight on to higher education after high school.

examples.ko: 성적이 좋으면 원하는 학교에 진학하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: With good grades, it's easier to get into the school you want.
After entering the school, I lived in a dorm.

explain: 진학하다는 지금 학교를 마치고 더 높은 단계의 학교로 가는 거예요. '입학'은 학교에 들어가는 일 자체이고, 진학은 다음 단계로 올라간다는 점이 달라요. 보통 '대학교에 진학하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 써요.

phrases.en: I want to go on to university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로의 학교 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about future school plans.
phrases.en_equiv: I want to go on to school

phrases.en: My younger sibling entered high school this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중학교를 마치고 다음 학교로 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving on after middle school.

phrases.en: I had a school-choice consultation with my teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 학교로 갈지 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when discussing which school to go to.

explain_en: 진학하다 is to finish one school and move up to the next level. Unlike '입학' (entering a school), it stresses stepping up to the next stage. It takes the particle 에: '대학교에 진학하다'.

en: to vote; to cast a ballot

examples.en: On election day I vote at the school.
Our class voted for a favorite song.
I will vote for the first time this time.
The number of people who vote keeps growing.
Opinions differed, so we voted and decided.
We voted with friends and chose a restaurant.

explain: 선거뿐 아니라 친구들끼리 메뉴를 고를 때도 '투표하다'를 가볍게 써요. 누구를 뽑는지 말하려면 '~에게 투표하다'라고 해요. 투표하러 가는 곳은 '투표소'예요.

phrases.en: I'm going to vote tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선거날에 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used around election day.

phrases.en: I voted for Minsu.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누구를 뽑았는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say who you voted for.

phrases.en: We decide the lunch menu by voting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍게 무엇을 고를 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used lightly for casual choices.

explain_en: It is not only for elections; friends also use it lightly when choosing a menu. To say who you vote for, use the pattern 'vote for someone'. The place you go to vote is the polling station.

examples.en: My father fishes at the river every weekend.
I went fishing at the sea yesterday.
Tomorrow I'm going fishing with a friend.

examples.ko: 낚시하는 동안 물고기가 한 마리도 안 잡혔어요.
examples.en: I didn't catch a single fish while fishing.
It's hard to fish when it rains.
I fished at the lake and came back home.

explain: '낚시를 하다'가 한 단어처럼 된 말이에요. '낚시하러 가다'는 낚시 자체가 목적일 때 많이 써요. 물고기를 실제로 '잡다'와는 달라서, 낚시하다고 해도 하나도 못 잡을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I go fishing with a friend on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낚시가 가는 목적일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when fishing is the purpose of going.

phrases.example: 저는 바다에서 낚시를 해 본 적이 있어요.
phrases.en: I have fished at the sea before.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낚시하다'를 두 말로 나눈 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The two-word form of 낚시하다.

phrases.en: There are many people fishing by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낚시를 하는 사람을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes people who are fishing.

explain_en: This is '낚시를 하다' ('do fishing') turned into one word. '낚시하러 가다' is the common way to say you go out to fish. It differs from '잡다' (to catch): you can 낚시하다 and still catch nothing.

examples.en: Our team won this round.
The game went to the third round.

examples.ko: 골프장에서 열여덟 홀 한 라운드를 돌았어요.
examples.en: I played one round of eighteen holes at the golf course.
You need points to move up to the next round.
The mood was heated from the very first round.
I made a mistake in the final round.

explain: 게임을 하다가 '한 판 더'라고 말하는 자리에 라운드도 쓸 수 있지만, 입말에서는 '판'이 더 흔해요. 권투·골프·오디션처럼 단계가 이어지는 경기에서는 '3라운드'처럼 숫자와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: Our team came from behind in the last round.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단계가 이어지는 경기의 마지막 단계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the final stage of a competition with several stages.

phrases.en: Who is in the next round?
phrases.nuance_ko: 오디션이나 대회에서 다음 단계를 물을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to ask about the next stage of an audition or contest.

phrases.en: Let's play one more round!
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임에서는 '라운드'보다 '판'이 입말에서 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In games, 'pan' is more common than 'round' in speech.

explain_en: Where you would say 'one more game' in everyday talk, Koreans usually use '판' rather than 'round'. 'Round' fits step-by-step contests like boxing, golf and auditions, and goes with numbers, as in 'round 3'.

examples.en: The child rides a tricycle around the park.

examples.ko: 세발자전거는 바퀴가 세 개라서 넘어지지 않아요.
examples.en: A tricycle has three wheels, so it doesn't fall over.
My nephew happily rides his tricycle around the yard.
The tricycle broke, so I fixed the wheel.

examples.ko: 두발자전거를 배우기 전에 세발자전거에 먼저 앉아 봤어요.
examples.en: Before learning a two-wheeled bike, I first sat on a tricycle.

examples.ko: 세발자전거도 이제 작아져서 아이가 못 타요.
examples.en: The tricycle has become too small now, so the child can't ride it.

explain: 바퀴가 세 개인 어린이용 자전거예요. 짝이 되는 말은 '두발자전거'이고, 두발자전거를 처음 배울 때는 '보조 바퀴'를 달기도 해요. '세 발'과 붙여서 한 단어처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I bought my child a tricycle for their birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부모가 아이에게 선물할 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when a parent gives a gift to a child.

phrases.en: The tricycle's wheel came off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바퀴가 세 개인 점을 떠올리며 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits with the fact that it has three wheels.

phrases.en: Now I ride a two-wheeled bike instead of a tricycle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세발자전거와 짝이 되는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart word to '세발자전거'.

explain_en: It is a children's bicycle with three wheels. Its counterpart is '두발자전거', and kids sometimes add '보조 바퀴' (training wheels) when first learning to ride one. It is written together as a single word.

examples.en: We did long-distance running in PE class today.
In long-distance running, you should start slowly.
I like sprints more than long-distance running.
My long-distance running time is better than last month.
After long-distance running, I drink enough water.

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 가을에 오래달리기 대회가 있어요.
examples.en: Our school has a long-distance running event in autumn.

explain: 학교 체육에서 많이 듣는 종목 이름이에요. 짧은 거리를 빨리 뛰는 '단거리 달리기'와 반대로 오래 쉬지 않고 뛰는 거예요. 한 단어라서 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: In P.E. class we did long-distance running on the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오래달리기'와 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with '오래달리기'.

phrases.en: We have a long-distance running test tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 체력을 재는 시험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for school fitness tests.

phrases.en: My long-distance running record has improved a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뛴 시간이나 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for your running time or result.

explain_en: This is an event name you often hear in school PE. It is the opposite of short sprints, meaning running for a long time without stopping. It is written as one word.

examples.en: I took the last runner's spot in the relay race at the sports day.
Teamwork is really important in a relay race.
Our class came first in the relay race.
I fell while practicing for the relay race.
I was picked as a relay runner, so I'm nervous.
When the relay race started, the cheering got louder.

explain: 학교 운동회에서 가장 인기 있는 종목 중 하나예요. '릴레이'라는 외래어도 쓰고, 운동 경기에서는 '계주'라고도 해요. '이어달리기를 하다', '이어달리기에 나가다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: We did a relay race on the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기를 한다는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you ran a relay.

phrases.en: I'm entering the relay race.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대표로 경기에 참가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when taking part as a competitor.

phrases.en: Our class won first place in the relay.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 경기에서 쓰는 같은 뜻의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A synonym used in sports contexts.

explain_en: It is one of the most popular events at school sports days. The loanword '릴레이' is also used, and in athletics the term '계주' is common. You say '이어달리기를 하다' or '이어달리기에 나가다'.

examples.en: That singer's low notes are really cool.
Speaking slowly in a low voice sounds comfortable.

examples.ko: 이 스피커는 저음을 잘 살려 줘요.
examples.en: This speaker brings out the low sounds well.
My voice cracked on the low notes while I was singing.

examples.ko: 형의 저음은 깊고 부드러워서 라디오에 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: My brother's low voice is deep and soft, so it suits the radio.

examples.ko: 저음도 고음도 잘 내는 사람이 부러워요.
examples.en: I envy people who can sing both low and high notes well.

explain: '고음'과 짝이 되는 말로, 소리의 높낮이를 말할 때 써요. '저음이 좋다', '저음을 내다'처럼 말해요. 사람 목소리에는 '낮은 목소리'도 같이 써요.

phrases.en: It's hard to sing low notes when singing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낮은 소리를 만들어 낼 때 '내다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '내다' is used when you produce a low sound.

phrases.en: That person speaks in a low voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 말하는 소리는 '저음'보다 '낮은 목소리'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a person's speaking voice, '낮은 목소리' sounds more natural than '저음'.

phrases.example: 이 노래는 고음과 저음이 다 있어요.
phrases.en: This song has both high and low notes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대되는 말인 '고음'과 같이 써서 소리의 차이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with its opposite '고음' to describe the range of sounds.

explain_en: It pairs with 고음 and describes how low a sound is. Typical use is 저음이 좋다 or 저음을 내다. For human voices, 낮은 목소리 is also used.

examples.en: My father is an owner-driver taxi driver.
I make my living running a private taxi.
An owner-driver taxi doesn't belong to a company.
At night it's hard to catch an owner-driver taxi.
I took a private taxi all the way to the airport.
The private taxi driver knows the roads well.

explain: 회사 소속이 아니라 기사 본인이 면허를 가지고 운행하는 택시예요. 회사에서 운영하는 '법인택시'와 구분해서 말해요. 보통 '개인택시 기사'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The private taxi driver was kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개인택시를 모는 사람을 말할 때 '기사님'으로 높여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the driver, politely called 기사님.

phrases.en: This car is a company taxi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에서 운영하는 택시로, 개인택시와 구분해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A taxi run by a company, contrasted with 개인택시.

phrases.en: I took a private taxi at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교통수단은 '타다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Transportation goes with the verb 타다.

explain_en: It is a taxi run by a driver who holds the license personally, not by a company. It is distinguished from '법인택시', which a company operates. People usually say '개인택시 기사'.

examples.en: I write down each day's schedule in my notebook.

examples.ko: 저는 그날그날 기분에 따라 옷을 골라요.
examples.en: I pick my clothes depending on my mood each day.

examples.ko: 오늘 할 일은 그날그날 끝내는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to finish each day's tasks on that same day.
Vegetable prices at the market differ from day to day.

examples.ko: 그날그날 배운 단어를 복습하면 잊어버리지 않아요.
examples.en: If you review the words you learn each day, you won't forget them.

examples.ko: 그날그날 먹고 싶은 음식을 골라서 먹어요.
examples.en: I choose and eat whatever I feel like eating each day.

explain: '매일'은 날마다 반복된다는 느낌이고, '그날그날'은 그날의 사정이나 기분에 맞춰 하루하루 달라진다는 느낌이 있어요. 그래서 '달라요, 다르다'와 자주 같이 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '그때그때'도 있어요.

phrases.en: I buy what I need as the need comes up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그날그날'은 하루 단위이고, '그때그때'는 하루가 아니어도 상황에 맞춰 달라진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '그날그날' is day by day, while '그때그때' means as each situation comes, not necessarily daily.
phrases.en_equiv: from time to time; as needed

phrases.en: My mood is different from day to day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '달라요'와 가장 자주 같이 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing is with 'differ'.

phrases.en: I always finish each day's tasks that day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하루에 해야 하는 일을 그날 처리한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means handling each day's tasks on the same day.

explain_en: '매일' stresses that something repeats every day, while '그날그날' means day by day, adjusting to that day's situation or mood. That is why it often appears with '달라요' (is different). A similar word is '그때그때' (depending on each moment).
